full.title: Orbital kaolinite signal
full.prompt: Is the signal from bedrock or from loose light-toned pebbles? Photograph both. Kaolinite usually needs long leaching by water. (Orbital CRISM, medium confidence: verify on the ground.)
full.source: Parente et al., CRISM dominant mineralogy of Jezero crater, Zenodo 5575824 (CC-BY-4.0); medium confidence

full.title: Onto thinly layered delta rock
full.prompt: Look for fine layering and grain-size changes; photograph a layer edge with a scale. Thin layers record how water flowed into the lake.
full.source: Stack et al. 2020, Photogeologic map of the Perseverance rover field site, Space Sci. Rev. 216:127 (CC-BY-4.0)

full.title: Crossing large wind ripples
full.prompt: Photograph ripple crests and note their direction; check for coarse grains on the crests. Records today's winds.
full.source: Stack et al. 2020, Photogeologic map of the Perseverance rover field site, Space Sci. Rev. 216:127 (CC-BY-4.0)

full.title: Orbital kaolinite signal again
full.prompt: Compare with the earlier patch: same rock? Is the signal from bedrock or from loose light-toned pebbles? Photograph both. Kaolinite usually needs long leaching by water. (Orbital CRISM, high confidence: verify on the ground.)
full.source: Parente et al., CRISM dominant mineralogy of Jezero crater, Zenodo 5575824 (CC-BY-4.0); high confidence

full.title: Orbital pyroxene signal
full.prompt: Note the rock texture (crystals, vesicles). Pyroxene marks volcanic rock: a baseline to compare with the water-altered rocks. (Orbital CRISM, medium confidence: verify on the ground.)
full.source: Parente et al., CRISM dominant mineralogy of Jezero crater, Zenodo 5575824 (CC-BY-4.0); medium confidence

skipA.title: Back on the smooth crater floor
skipA.prompt: Look for bedrock poking through the loose cover; photograph any exposed patch. Tells us what lies under the regolith.
skipA.source: Stack et al. 2020, Photogeologic map of the Perseverance rover field site, Space Sci. Rev. 216:127 (CC-BY-4.0)
